findings.text: Upheld as a defect (Q6, a disagreement in behaviour with the neighbouring rule; also Q2). Line 2008 of the diff adds this line. RECEIVED_VISIBLE's EXISTS joins `a.alias = x.remote_alias` with no tie to `l.bound_alias`, and the scope's alias it is passed is `hostLedAliasOf` (contribute.ts:115-127), the project's first host-led alias in alphabetical order. `aliasBoundTo` and `boundAliasesOf` (levels.ts:79-106) both require `a.alias = l.bound_alias`. So for a project with two host-led aliases bound under the second, search, browse and get show the copies under the unbound alias and hide the bound ones. This is the same disagreement round 3 upheld, still standing in a second reader.

Upheld as a defect (Q2, logic duplicated, not boilerplate). The diff adds `parseEntryUid` here (diff.patch:8480). It writes the entry-uid grammar a second time beside src/team/validate.ts:53's `parseEntryUid`, a file this diff touches. The two regexes have already diverged: this one accepts any alias and any 36 characters of [0-9a-f-], while the server's requires a host-led alias. One shared parser, in contract.ts or beside `entryUid` in sharing/types.ts, would do, as was done for `entryBytes`.

Kept as an advisory (Q2). `aliasBoundTo` now agrees with `boundAliasesOf`, but it repeats that query with one more condition, and the two are kept in step by hand. Both are short SQL statements that now give the same answer, so this is a maintenance risk, not a wrong result.

Kept as an advisory (Q6, filed as advisory). The `applied` row's reason uses `agentName(remote.member.name)` with no member-id fallback, while author.ts:55 has one and ADR 0027's bullet says both do. The only effect is the marker text when the name is empty.

Kept as an advisory (Q2/Q6). The main path drops all pending rows of the uid, and the hourly path drops only rows up to the applied seq. The two rules differ, but the risk and data gates checked each one as correct for its own path.

Kept as an advisory (Q9). The `parsed.alias !== null` guard here and the one at outbound.ts:744 are unreachable once scope is project. They exist only because the parser's return type is not a discriminated union. They hide no cause, so they stay advisory.

Upheld as a defect (Q3, a preserve criterion that does not hold for a test it names). AC-85 (preserve) is still live in probes/criteria.md:13. Its text allows only the two configured-server sentences of this file to change. The diff also changes the saveSettings call, the two signature regexes, and adds the Servers and dock cases, so AC-85's 'passes unchanged' is false for this file. AC-92 names those changes, but AC-85 has not been retired or restated, and the gate cannot waive it. The person has to retire or restate AC-85.

Kept as an advisory (boundary hardening, personal-data). On the own-revision path, the member id goes into GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL as the server sent it, without `checkComponent`. Only a hostile server could exploit it.
Kept as an advisory (public-api). Pull-page items are not shape-checked where they enter, and the answer body has no size cap. Path components are checked, and a throw sets the row aside.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). A received memory is filed under any enabled project holding the alias, with no `aliasBoundTo` check. The brief and the prompt keep the row out, and only the receiving member can see it.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). Received memories become ordinary rows, and readers outside the diff (memory_search, consolidation neighbours) apply no mute or binding check. Those readers are debt the diff did not write.
Kept as an advisory (personal-data). After a restore, deleting an unlisted server's copies waits for a manual `sync --once`, and the CLI tells the person to run it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). `--code` on argv still exposes the invitation code to shell history and `ps`. A no-echo prompt exists and the usage text names it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). Remove forgets the token only locally, and the person is told that the device stays on the server until an admin revokes it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). The resume and add confirmations act on the current state, not on the preview the person was shown. Nothing beyond the policy is sent.

Upheld as a defect (Q7, a hidden control at a mandatory width). The diff adds this line (diff.patch:24604). The action group is `flex flex-none flex-wrap`, so it cannot shrink and its buttons do not wrap. At 360 in the held state, Remove… is off the card's edge: the row shows only Resume…, Mute and a clipped Rejoin…, so it offers no way to remove the server. Evidence: review/ui/settings-held@360-dark.png (checked), listed in review/inputs.json's captures, and review/ui/settings-muted@360-dark.png.

Upheld as a defect (Q1, AC-90's Sharing card texts naming the server give a wrong fact). The diff adds this line (diff.patch:7448). It reads any `server:` change whose new value is empty as 'removed' and any other as 'added'. But `muteServer` (src/sync/join.ts:379-386) logs an unmute as `server:<id>` with new '' and a mute with new 'mute'. So an unmute shows as 'server … removed' and a mute as 'server … added', as the capture shows after the script cancelled Remove…. Evidence: review/ui/settings-one@1280-dark.png and review/ui/settings-one@360-dark.png, listed in review/inputs.json.

Kept as an advisory. The held state is declared and captured. Only its count sub-branch (holdLine with n withdrawals) has no capture, and that is not a declared state that is missing. Evidence: review/ui/settings-held@1280-dark.png.

Kept as an advisory. Stale refusal toasts stay on screen into the next states, partly because of the capture's pacing. They crowd the screen but cover no control the states need. Evidence: review/ui/settings-confirming@1280-dark.png.

Kept as an advisory. Under 640px the nav footer's sentence about the environment narrowing sharing does not appear. The Sharing card's own help still states the ceiling. Evidence: review/ui/settings-empty@360-dark.png.

Kept as an advisory (Q1/Q4). The 'held pull answered at once' rule measures the time since the last answer, so the back-off does not double as spec.md:187 says. The server's hold bounds the loop, and status shows it.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). `INDEXED BY sharing_memories_updated` fails on a store that lacks the index. ADR 0027:87 limits this to unreleased development stores.

Kept as an advisory (Q1/Q3). The re-index skips a received project folder that has no manifest, so a later tombstone leaves its file on disk. Only a manifest removed by hand gets here, and `share server remove` deletes the whole folder. A log line would make the leftover visible.

Upheld as a defect (Q2, the data model's binding read differently). ADR 0027:58, :60 and :96 make `boundAliasesOf`'s rule (`a.alias = l.bound_alias`) the binding that every reader of received project entries uses, and src/retrieve/received.ts:48 reads it that way. RECEIVED_VISIBLE, which the diff adds (diff.patch:1997-2008), takes `x.remote_alias IS ?` with the scope alias from `hostLedAliasOf` (the first host-led alias by name, contribute.ts:115), and its EXISTS accepts any alias of the project, never `l.bound_alias`. Checked in the code: for a project with two remotes, copies under the bound alias are hidden, and copies under an alias no pull refreshes are shown.

Kept as an advisory (Q1). The sync runs its own SQL over the knowledge module's tables, with no boundary test for it. This was carried from round 2 and judged advisory there. The base draws no explicit rule that it breaks.
Kept as an advisory (Q3). `RESULT_SHAPES.refusal` omits the optional `accepted` and `retryAfterSec` that `RefusalShape` declares and the client reads. This was carried from round 2.

Kept as an advisory (Q6, placement). The writer of the entry uid's grammar is in the sharing leaf and its parser is in the sync's conflict module. The duplication behind it is upheld as a defect under code-quality, so here it stays a placement advisory.
